claim: LRRK2 variants associated with Parkinson's disease (PD) and Crohn's disease lead to increased phosphorylation of its Rab substrates.
source: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) variants associated with Parkinson's disease (PD) and Crohn's disease lead to increased phosphorylation of its Rab substrates.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about LRRK2 variants and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Perturbations in cellular homeostasis including lysosomal damage can increase LRRK2 activity and localization to lysosomes.
source: While it has been recently shown that perturbations in cellular homeostasis including lysosomal damage can increase LRRK2 activity and localization to lysosomes, the molecular mechanisms by which LRRK2 activity is regulated have remained poorly defined.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work in the introduction section.

claim: Rab12 is a novel modulator of LRRK2-dependent phosphorylation of Rab10.
source: We performed a targeted siRNA screen to identify regulators of LRRK2 activity and identified Rab12 as a novel modulator of LRRK2-dependent phosphorylation of one of its substrates, Rab10.
evidence: This claim is supported by the siRNA screen data presented in Figure 1A showing that RAB12 knockdown significantly reduced Rab10 phosphorylation.

claim: Rab12 is actively recruited to damaged lysosomes.
source: Using a combination of imaging and immunopurification methods to isolate lysosomes, we demonstrated that Rab12 is actively recruited to damaged lysosomes and leads to a local and LRRK2-dependent increase in Rab10 phosphorylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 3C-E showing increased Rab12 levels on lysosomes following LLOMe treatment.

claim: Rab12 recruitment to damaged lysosomes leads to a local and LRRK2-dependent increase in Rab10 phosphorylation.
source: Using a combination of imaging and immunopurification methods to isolate lysosomes, we demonstrated that Rab12 is actively recruited to damaged lysosomes and leads to a local and LRRK2-dependent increase in Rab10 phosphorylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 3A showing increased pT73 Rab10 on lysosomes following LLOMe treatment in WT but not RAB12 KO cells.

claim: PD-linked variants LRRK2 R1441G and VPS35 D620N lead to increased recruitment of LRRK2 to the lysosome.
source: PD-linked variants, including LRRK2 R1441G and VPS35 D620N, lead to increased recruitment of LRRK2 to the lysosome and a local elevation in lysosomal levels of pT73 Rab10.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 4D showing increased LRRK2 levels on lysosomes in LRRK2 R1441G and VPS35 D620N KI cells.

claim: PD-linked variants LRRK2 R1441G and VPS35 D620N lead to a local elevation in lysosomal levels of pT73 Rab10.
source: PD-linked variants, including LRRK2 R1441G and VPS35 D620N, lead to increased recruitment of LRRK2 to the lysosome and a local elevation in lysosomal levels of pT73 Rab10.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 4B and 4C showing increased pT73 Rab10 on lysosomes in LRRK2 R1441G and VPS35 D620N KI cells.

claim: Coding variants in LRRK2 can cause monogenic Parkinson's disease.
source: Coding variants in LRRK2 can cause monogenic Parkinson's disease (PD), and coding and non-coding variants in LRRK2 are associated with increased risk for developing sporadic PD and Crohn's disease (Blauwendraat et al., 2020; Hui et al., 2018; Kluss et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Coding and non-coding variants in LRRK2 are associated with increased risk for developing sporadic PD and Crohn's disease.
source: Coding variants in LRRK2 can cause monogenic Parkinson's disease (PD), and coding and non-coding variants in LRRK2 are associated with increased risk for developing sporadic PD and Crohn's disease (Blauwendraat et al., 2020; Hui et al., 2018; Kluss et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The majority of pathogenic LRRK2 variants cluster within its Roc-COR GTPase tandem domain or kinase domain.
source: The majority of pathogenic LRRK2 variants cluster within its Roc-COR (Ras of complex proteins/C-terminal of Roc) GTPase tandem domain or kinase domain and contribute to disease risk by ultimately increasing LRRK2's kinase activity (Alessi and Sammler, 2018; Kalogeropulou et al., 2022; Sheng et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Pathogenic LRRK2 variants contribute to disease risk by ultimately increasing LRRK2's kinase activity.
source: The majority of pathogenic LRRK2 variants cluster within its Roc-COR (Ras of complex proteins/C-terminal of Roc) GTPase tandem domain or kinase domain and contribute to disease risk by ultimately increasing LRRK2's kinase activity (Alessi and Sammler, 2018; Kalogeropulou et al., 2022; Sheng et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: LRRK2 phosphorylates a subset of Rab GTPases, including Rab10 and Rab12.
source: LRRK2 phosphorylates a subset of Rab GTPases, including Rab10 and Rab12.
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Excessive Rab phosphorylation can perturb interactions between Rabs and downstream effectors.
source: Excessive Rab phosphorylation can perturb interactions between Rabs and downstream effectors, which impairs various aspects of membrane trafficking including lysosomal function (Pfeffer, 2018; Steger et al., 2017; Steger et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Excessive Rab phosphorylation impairs various aspects of membrane trafficking including lysosomal function.
source: Excessive Rab phosphorylation can perturb interactions between Rabs and downstream effectors, which impairs various aspects of membrane trafficking including lysosomal function (Pfeffer, 2018; Steger et al., 2017; Steger et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: LRRK2 localizes primarily to the cytosol in an inactive state.
source: LRRK2 localizes primarily to the cytosol in an inactive state, and higher-order oligomerization and membrane recruitment appear to be required for LRRK2 activation and Rab phosphorylation (Berger et al., 2010; Biskup et al., 2006; Greggio et al., 2008; Schapansky et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Higher-order oligomerization and membrane recruitment appear to be required for LRRK2 activation and Rab phosphorylation.
source: LRRK2 localizes primarily to the cytosol in an inactive state, and higher-order oligomerization and membrane recruitment appear to be required for LRRK2 activation and Rab phosphorylation (Berger et al., 2010; Biskup et al., 2006; Greggio et al., 2008; Schapansky et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Interactions between LRRK2 and its phosphorylated Rab substrates help maintain LRRK2 on membranes.
source: Recent work suggests that interactions between LRRK2 and its phosphorylated Rab substrates help maintain LRRK2 on membranes and result in a cooperative, feed-forward mechanism to promote additional Rab phosphorylation (Vides et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Interactions between LRRK2 and its phosphorylated Rab substrates result in a cooperative, feed-forward mechanism to promote additional Rab phosphorylation.
source: Recent work suggests that interactions between LRRK2 and its phosphorylated Rab substrates help maintain LRRK2 on membranes and result in a cooperative, feed-forward mechanism to promote additional Rab phosphorylation (Vides et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Endolysosomal genes that modify PD risk can increase LRRK2 activation and phosphorylation of its Rab substrates.
source: Endolysosomal genes that modify PD risk and lysosomal damage can also increase LRRK2 activation and phosphorylation of its Rab substrates (Bonet-Ponce et al., 2020; Eguchi et al., 2018; Herbst et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2018; Mir et al., 2018; Purlyte et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lysosomal damage can increase LRRK2 activation and phosphorylation of its Rab substrates.
source: Endolysosomal genes that modify PD risk and lysosomal damage can also increase LRRK2 activation and phosphorylation of its Rab substrates (Bonet-Ponce et al., 2020; Eguchi et al., 2018; Herbst et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2018; Mir et al., 2018; Purlyte et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab29 and VPS35 are genetically associated with PD.
source: Rab29 and the retromer subunit VPS35, proteins that are genetically associated with PD and play key roles in lysosomal function by regulating sorting between the endolysosomal system and the trans-Golgi network, can modulate LRRK2 activity, as overexpression of Rab29 or expression of the pathogenic VPS35 D620N variant lead to significantly elevated LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 and other Rab substrates (Liu et al., 2018; Mir et al., 2018; Purlyte et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab29 and VPS35 play key roles in lysosomal function by regulating sorting between the endolysosomal system and the trans-Golgi network.
source: Rab29 and the retromer subunit VPS35, proteins that are genetically associated with PD and play key roles in lysosomal function by regulating sorting between the endolysosomal system and the trans-Golgi network, can modulate LRRK2 activity, as overexpression of Rab29 or expression of the pathogenic VPS35 D620N variant lead to significantly elevated LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 and other Rab substrates (Liu et al., 2018; Mir et al., 2018; Purlyte et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Overexpression of Rab29 leads to significantly elevated LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 and other Rab substrates.
source: Rab29 and the retromer subunit VPS35, proteins that are genetically associated with PD and play key roles in lysosomal function by regulating sorting between the endolysosomal system and the trans-Golgi network, can modulate LRRK2 activity, as overexpression of Rab29 or expression of the pathogenic VPS35 D620N variant lead to significantly elevated LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 and other Rab substrates (Liu et al., 2018; Mir et al., 2018; Purlyte et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Expression of the pathogenic VPS35 D620N variant leads to significantly elevated LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 and other Rab substrates.
source: Rab29 and the retromer subunit VPS35, proteins that are genetically associated with PD and play key roles in lysosomal function by regulating sorting between the endolysosomal system and the trans-Golgi network, can modulate LRRK2 activity, as overexpression of Rab29 or expression of the pathogenic VPS35 D620N variant lead to significantly elevated LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 and other Rab substrates (Liu et al., 2018; Mir et al., 2018; Purlyte et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: LRRK2 kinase activity appears to be increased in nonhereditary idiopathic PD patients.
source: LRRK2 kinase activity also appears to be increased in nonhereditary idiopathic PD patients (Di Maio et al., 2018; Fraser et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2021), and emerging data suggest that lysosomal damage more broadly may be a common trigger for LRRK2 activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lysosomotropic agents that disrupt the endolysosomal pH gradient or puncture lysosomal membranes enhance LRRK2 recruitment to damaged lysosomes.
source: Lysosomotropic agents that disrupt the endolysosomal pH gradient or puncture lysosomal membranes enhance LRRK2 recruitment to damaged lysosomes and result in increased Rab10 phosphorylation (Bonet-Ponce et al., 2020; Eguchi et al., 2018; Herbst et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lysosomotropic agents that disrupt the endolysosomal pH gradient or puncture lysosomal membranes result in increased Rab10 phosphorylation.
source: Lysosomotropic agents that disrupt the endolysosomal pH gradient or puncture lysosomal membranes enhance LRRK2 recruitment to damaged lysosomes and result in increased Rab10 phosphorylation (Bonet-Ponce et al., 2020; Eguchi et al., 2018; Herbst et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RAB12 knockdown significantly reduced Rab10 phosphorylation in A549 cells.
source: RAB12 was the only hit gene whose knockdown significantly reduced Rab10 phosphorylation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is directly supported by the siRNA screen data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: RAB12 knockdown reduced gene expression and led to a reduction in Rab12 protein levels.
source: We confirmed that RAB12 knockdown reduced gene expression and led to a reduction in Rab12 protein levels (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 1C-E.

claim: RAB12 knockdown did not impact the levels of LRRK2 or Rab10.
source: RAB12 knockdown did not impact the levels of LRRK2 or Rab10, suggesting that Rab12 mediates Rab10 phosphorylation by regulating LRRK2's activity rather than the stability of LRRK2 or Rab10 (Figure 1B, D, and F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot and MSD data shown in Figure 1B, D, F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Rab12 mediates Rab10 phosphorylation by regulating LRRK2's activity rather than the stability of LRRK2 or Rab10.
source: RAB12 knockdown did not impact the levels of LRRK2 or Rab10, suggesting that Rab12 mediates Rab10 phosphorylation by regulating LRRK2's activity rather than the stability of LRRK2 or Rab10 (Figure 1B, D, and F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that RAB12 knockdown reduces Rab10 phosphorylation without affecting LRRK2 or Rab10 protein levels.

claim: Rab29 does not regulate LRRK2 activity under endogenous expression conditions.
source: We also confirmed previous observations that Rab29 does not regulate LRRK2 activity under endogenous expression conditions as RAB29 knockdown or genetic deletion did not impact Rab10 phosphorylation in A549 cells (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 showing no effect of RAB29 knockdown or deletion on Rab10 phosphorylation.

claim: Loss of Rab12 significantly impairs Rab10 phosphorylation at T73.
source: We demonstrated that loss of Rab12 significantly impairs Rab10 phosphorylation at T73, showing a comparable reduction to that observed with loss of LRRK2 (Figure 2A and B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by MSD and western blot data in RAB12 KO cells shown in Figure 2A-B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Total Rab10 levels were not reduced with RAB12 deletion.
source: Total Rab10 levels were not reduced with RAB12 deletion and, in fact, were elevated in two out of three RAB12 KO clones assessed, confirming that the impact of loss of Rab12 on Rab10 phosphorylation cannot be explained by an effect on the protein levels of Rab10 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Overexpression of either WT Rab12 or Rab12 S106A restored Rab10 phosphorylation at T73.
source: Overexpression of either WT Rab12 or Rab12 S106A restored Rab10 phosphorylation at T73 and did not impact LRRK2 levels (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by MSD data in doxycycline-inducible cell lines shown in Figure 2E-F.

claim: LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab12 does not contribute to LRRK2 activation.
source: Overexpression of either WT Rab12 or Rab12 S106A restored Rab10 phosphorylation at T73 and did not impact LRRK2 levels (Figure 2E and F). This finding was further confirmed using Rab12 S106A KI cells generated using CRISPR-Cas9 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that both WT and phospho-deficient Rab12 S106A equally restore Rab10 phosphorylation.

claim: Rab12 is required to mediate LRRK2 activation in response to LRRK2 R1441G variant.
source: Rab10 phosphorylation was significantly reduced with RAB12 knockdown in LRRK2 R1441G KI and VPS35 D620N KI A549 cells (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 2G showing reduced Rab10 phosphorylation with RAB12 knockdown in LRRK2 R1441G cells.

claim: Rab12 is required to mediate LRRK2 activation in response to VPS35 D620N variant.
source: Rab10 phosphorylation was significantly reduced with RAB12 knockdown in LRRK2 R1441G KI and VPS35 D620N KI A549 cells (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 2G showing reduced Rab10 phosphorylation with RAB12 knockdown in VPS35 D620N cells.

claim: LLOMe treatment led to a significant increase in Rab10 phosphorylation in WT cells.
source: We confirmed that LLOMe treatment led to a significant increase in Rab10 phosphorylation in WT cells and demonstrated this effect was abolished in RAB12 KO cells (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by MSD data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The effect of LLOMe on Rab10 phosphorylation was abolished in RAB12 KO cells.
source: We confirmed that LLOMe treatment led to a significant increase in Rab10 phosphorylation in WT cells and demonstrated this effect was abolished in RAB12 KO cells (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by MSD data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: LLOMe treatment induced lysosomal membrane rupture as evidenced by increased galectin-3 levels on isolated lysosomes.
source: Lysosomes isolated from WT and RAB12 KO A549 cells treated with vehicle or LLOMe (1 mM) for 2 hr displayed increased levels of endogenous galectin-3 (Gal3), validating that LLOMe treatment induced lysosomal membrane rupture and exposed beta-galactosides normally present in the lumen of lysosomes (Figure 3A; Jia et al., 2020; Maejima et al., 2013; Paz et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data showing increased Gal3 on isolated lysosomes in Figure 3A and citations to previous literature.

claim: LLOMe treatment reduced the levels of LAMP1 in isolated lysosomes.
source: While LLOMe treatment reduced the levels of lysosomal-associated membrane protein 1 (LAMP1) in isolated lysosomes, the levels and localization of TMEM192-3x-HA, the lysosomal membrane protein used to isolate lysosomes, were not significantly impacted by LLOMe treatment (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The levels and localization of TMEM192-3x-HA were not significantly impacted by LLOMe treatment.
source: While LLOMe treatment reduced the levels of lysosomal-associated membrane protein 1 (LAMP1) in isolated lysosomes, the levels and localization of TMEM192-3x-HA, the lysosomal membrane protein used to isolate lysosomes, were not significantly impacted by LLOMe treatment (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot and imaging data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: LLOMe treatment increased phosphorylation of Rab10 on isolated lysosomes from WT cells.
source: Using this method, we showed that LLOMe treatment increased phosphorylation of Rab10 on isolated lysosomes from WT cells but failed to increase Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes from RAB12 KO cells, demonstrating that Rab12 is a critical regulator of Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes following lysosomal damage (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data from isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 3A.

claim: LLOMe treatment failed to increase Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes from RAB12 KO cells.
source: Using this method, we showed that LLOMe treatment increased phosphorylation of Rab10 on isolated lysosomes from WT cells but failed to increase Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes from RAB12 KO cells, demonstrating that Rab12 is a critical regulator of Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes following lysosomal damage (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data from isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Rab12 is a critical regulator of Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes following lysosomal damage.
source: Using this method, we showed that LLOMe treatment increased phosphorylation of Rab10 on isolated lysosomes from WT cells but failed to increase Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes from RAB12 KO cells, demonstrating that Rab12 is a critical regulator of Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes following lysosomal damage (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data from isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A proportion of Rab10 is localized to lysosomes basally and in response to lysosomal damage.
source: While Rab10 has been reported to primarily localize to the Golgi and endosomes, our data show that a proportion of Rab10 is localized to lysosomes basally and in response to lysosomal damage (Berndsen et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by the lysosome immunopurification data and imaging data showing Rab10 on lysosomes.

claim: LLOMe treatment significantly increased colocalization between pT73 Rab10 and LAMP1 in WT cells.
source: LLOMe treatment significantly increased colocalization between pT73 Rab10 and LAMP1 in WT cells but had no effect in RAB12 KO cells, confirming that Rab12 is required for Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes in response to membrane rupture (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: LLOMe treatment had no effect on colocalization between pT73 Rab10 and LAMP1 in RAB12 KO cells.
source: LLOMe treatment significantly increased colocalization between pT73 Rab10 and LAMP1 in WT cells but had no effect in RAB12 KO cells, confirming that Rab12 is required for Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes in response to membrane rupture (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Rab12 is required for Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes in response to membrane rupture.
source: LLOMe treatment significantly increased colocalization between pT73 Rab10 and LAMP1 in WT cells but had no effect in RAB12 KO cells, confirming that Rab12 is required for Rab10 phosphorylation on lysosomes in response to membrane rupture (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: LLOMe treatment significantly increased the levels of Rab12 on lysosomes.
source: Consistent with this idea, treatment with LLOMe significantly increased the levels of Rab12 on lysosomes assessed by western blot analysis from isolated lysosomes and by confocal imaging (Figure 3C–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot and imaging data shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: LLOMe treatment significantly increased the colocalization of Rab12 with the lysosomal marker LAMP1.
source: Further imaging analysis revealed that LLOMe treatment significantly increased the colocalization of Rab12 with the lysosomal marker LAMP1, but not with the Golgi marker GM130, as quantified by Pearson's correlation coefficient (PCC), and this colocalization was preserved upon nocodazole-induced microtubule depolymerization (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data and PCC analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: LLOMe treatment did not significantly increase the colocalization of Rab12 with the Golgi marker GM130.
source: Further imaging analysis revealed that LLOMe treatment significantly increased the colocalization of Rab12 with the lysosomal marker LAMP1, but not with the Golgi marker GM130, as quantified by Pearson's correlation coefficient (PCC), and this colocalization was preserved upon nocodazole-induced microtubule depolymerization (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data and PCC analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Rab12 recruitment to damaged lysosomes was not impacted by LRRK2 deletion.
source: Rab12 recruitment to damaged lysosomes was not impacted by LRRK2 deletion as Rab12 levels were similarly increased on lysosomes from WT and LRRK2 KO cells following lysosomal membrane permeabilization (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Rab12 is an upstream regulator of LRRK2's lysosomal localization and activity.
source: These data demonstrate that lysosomal membrane damage increases Rab12 localization to lysosomes and that this occurs in an LRRK2-independent manner, supporting the idea that Rab12 is an upstream regulator of LRRK2's lysosomal localization and activity.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that Rab12 recruitment to lysosomes occurs independently of LRRK2.

claim: Approximately 1% of total Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline.
source: Western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes showed that approximately 1% of total Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline and that this increased to approximately 1.5% following LLOMe treatment, while our imaging-based analysis revealed that approximately 12% of overexpressed Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline and increased to approximately 14% upon LLOMe treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Approximately 1.5% of total Rab12 was present on lysosomes following LLOMe treatment.
source: Western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes showed that approximately 1% of total Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline and that this increased to approximately 1.5% following LLOMe treatment, while our imaging-based analysis revealed that approximately 12% of overexpressed Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline and increased to approximately 14% upon LLOMe treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Approximately 12% of overexpressed Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline.
source: Western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes showed that approximately 1% of total Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline and that this increased to approximately 1.5% following LLOMe treatment, while our imaging-based analysis revealed that approximately 12% of overexpressed Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline and increased to approximately 14% upon LLOMe treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging-based analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Approximately 14% of overexpressed Rab12 was present on lysosomes upon LLOMe treatment.
source: Western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes showed that approximately 1% of total Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline and that this increased to approximately 1.5% following LLOMe treatment, while our imaging-based analysis revealed that approximately 12% of overexpressed Rab12 was present on lysosomes at baseline and increased to approximately 14% upon LLOMe treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging-based analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Rab12 and LRRK2 showed a diffuse localization under baseline conditions.
source: Rab12 and LRRK2 showed a diffuse localization under baseline conditions, while LLOMe treatment increased the recruitment of Rab12 and LRRK2 to vesicular structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: LLOMe treatment increased the recruitment of Rab12 and LRRK2 to vesicular structures.
source: Rab12 and LRRK2 showed a diffuse localization under baseline conditions, while LLOMe treatment increased the recruitment of Rab12 and LRRK2 to vesicular structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Rab12 colocalization with LRRK2 increased over time following LLOMe treatment.
source: Rab12 colocalization with LRRK2 increased over time following LLOMe treatment, supporting potential coordinated recruitment of these proteins to lysosomes upon damage (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by live-cell imaging data and PCC analysis shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: LLOMe treatment significantly increased the colocalization of LRRK2 with the lysosomal marker LAMP1.
source: LLOMe treatment also significantly increased the colocalization of LRRK2 with the lysosomal marker LAMP1 but not with the Golgi marker GM130 (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data and PCC analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: LLOMe treatment did not significantly increase the colocalization of LRRK2 with the Golgi marker GM130.
source: LLOMe treatment also significantly increased the colocalization of LRRK2 with the lysosomal marker LAMP1 but not with the Golgi marker GM130 (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data and PCC analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Lysosomal levels of LRRK2 were increased by approximately 2.5-fold following treatment with LLOMe in WT cells.
source: Lysosomal levels of LRRK2 were increased by approximately 2.5-fold following treatment with LLOMe in WT cells, and loss of Rab12 abrogated this LLOMe-induced increase (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Loss of Rab12 abrogated the LLOMe-induced increase in lysosomal LRRK2 levels.
source: Lysosomal levels of LRRK2 were increased by approximately 2.5-fold following treatment with LLOMe in WT cells, and loss of Rab12 abrogated this LLOMe-induced increase (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Rab12 is required to facilitate LRRK2 localization to lysosomes following membrane damage.
source: These data show that Rab12 is required to facilitate LRRK2 localization to lysosomes following membrane damage.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data showing that loss of Rab12 prevents LLOMe-induced LRRK2 recruitment to lysosomes.

claim: Expression of LRRK2 R1441G led to an increase in Rab10 phosphorylation on isolated lysosomes at baseline.
source: Expression of LRRK2 R1441G or VPS35 D620N led to an increase in Rab10 phosphorylation on isolated lysosomes at baseline, and the phosphorylation of Rab10 on lysosomes was further increased following LLOMe treatment (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Expression of VPS35 D620N led to an increase in Rab10 phosphorylation on isolated lysosomes at baseline.
source: Expression of LRRK2 R1441G or VPS35 D620N led to an increase in Rab10 phosphorylation on isolated lysosomes at baseline, and the phosphorylation of Rab10 on lysosomes was further increased following LLOMe treatment (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The phosphorylation of Rab10 on lysosomes was further increased following LLOMe treatment in LRRK2 R1441G and VPS35 D620N cells.
source: Expression of LRRK2 R1441G or VPS35 D620N led to an increase in Rab10 phosphorylation on isolated lysosomes at baseline, and the phosphorylation of Rab10 on lysosomes was further increased following LLOMe treatment (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The levels of LRRK2 on lysosomes were significantly increased in untreated LRRK2 R1441G KI cells.
source: The levels of LRRK2 on lysosomes were significantly increased in untreated LRRK2 R1441G KI cells and VPS35 D620N KI cells, suggesting that enhanced localization of LRRK2 to lysosomes and proximity to its Rab substrates may contribute to the elevated Rab10 phosphorylation observed on lysosomes at baseline in these cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The levels of LRRK2 on lysosomes were significantly increased in untreated VPS35 D620N KI cells.
source: The levels of LRRK2 on lysosomes were significantly increased in untreated LRRK2 R1441G KI cells and VPS35 D620N KI cells, suggesting that enhanced localization of LRRK2 to lysosomes and proximity to its Rab substrates may contribute to the elevated Rab10 phosphorylation observed on lysosomes at baseline in these cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of isolated lysosomes shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Enhanced localization of LRRK2 to lysosomes and proximity to its Rab substrates may contribute to the elevated Rab10 phosphorylation observed on lysosomes at baseline in LRRK2 R1441G and VPS35 D620N cells.
source: The levels of LRRK2 on lysosomes were significantly increased in untreated LRRK2 R1441G KI cells and VPS35 D620N KI cells, suggesting that enhanced localization of LRRK2 to lysosomes and proximity to its Rab substrates may contribute to the elevated Rab10 phosphorylation observed on lysosomes at baseline in these cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the correlation between increased LRRK2 on lysosomes and increased Rab10 phosphorylation.

claim: Rab12 regulates LRRK2 localization to lysosomes upon damage.
source: Together, these results suggest that Rab12 regulates LRRK2 localization to lysosomes upon damage and that this may be a conserved mechanism also employed to contribute to LRRK2 activation in response to PD-linked variants.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data showing that Rab12 is required for LRRK2 recruitment to lysosomes following LLOMe treatment.

claim: Rab12-mediated LRRK2 localization to lysosomes may be a conserved mechanism employed to contribute to LRRK2 activation in response to PD-linked variants.
source: Together, these results suggest that Rab12 regulates LRRK2 localization to lysosomes upon damage and that this may be a conserved mechanism also employed to contribute to LRRK2 activation in response to PD-linked variants.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that both lysosomal damage and PD-linked variants increase LRRK2 on lysosomes.

claim: A recent CRISPR-based genome-wide screen for modifiers of Rab10 phosphorylation identified RAB12 as a top hit.
source: A recent CRISPR-based genome-wide screen for modifiers of Rab10 phosphorylation also identified RAB12 as a top hit, providing additional validation that Rab12 is a key regulator of LRRK2 activation (Dhekne et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent publication.

claim: Rab12 recruits LRRK2 to the lysosome and enhances its activity on lysosomal membranes by increasing LRRK2's local concentration near Rab10 and potentially other Rab substrates.
source: We propose a model in which Rab12 recruits LRRK2 to the lysosome and enhances its activity on lysosomal membranes by increasing LRRK2's local concentration near Rab10 and potentially other Rab substrates (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Exogenously expressed Rab29 is capable of activating LRRK2 at the trans-Golgi or at additional membranes when artificially anchored there.
source: Previous studies suggested that another LRRK2 substrate, Rab29, can regulate LRRK2's kinase activity and showed that exogenously expressed Rab29 is capable of activating LRRK2 at the trans-Golgi or at additional membranes when artificially anchored there (Purlyte et al., 2018; Gomez et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RAB29 deletion minimally impacted LRRK2-dependent Rab10 phosphorylation.
source: However, these studies relied on overexpression of Rab29 to increase LRRK2 activity, and analyses of RAB29 KO cellular models or mice showed that RAB29 deletion minimally impacted LRRK2-dependent Rab10 phosphorylation (Kalogeropulou et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rab12 regulates LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 under endogenous expression conditions.
source: Here, we used endogenous expression conditions to demonstrate that Rab12, but not Rab29, regulates LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 and that Rab12 regulates the localization and activation of LRRK2 on lysosomes upon lysosomal stress.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data presented in the manuscript using endogenous expression systems.

claim: Rab29 does not regulate LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 under endogenous expression conditions.
source: Here, we used endogenous expression conditions to demonstrate that Rab12, but not Rab29, regulates LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 and that Rab12 regulates the localization and activation of LRRK2 on lysosomes upon lysosomal stress.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data presented in the manuscript using endogenous expression systems.

claim: Rab12 regulates the localization and activation of LRRK2 on lysosomes upon lysosomal stress.
source: Here, we used endogenous expression conditions to demonstrate that Rab12, but not Rab29, regulates LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of Rab10 and that Rab12 regulates the localization and activation of LRRK2 on lysosomes upon lysosomal stress.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The PD-linked pathogenic LRRK2 variant R1441G increases LRRK2 activity.
source: The PD-linked pathogenic LRRK2 variant R1441G, which lies outside of LRRK2's kinase domain, and the VPS35 D620N variant have been shown in previous studies and confirmed here to increase LRRK2 activity (Liu et al., 2018; Mir et al., 2018; Purlyte et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and data in the current manuscript.

claim: The VPS35 D620N variant increases LRRK2 activity.
source: The PD-linked pathogenic LRRK2 variant R1441G, which lies outside of LRRK2's kinase domain, and the VPS35 D620N variant have been shown in previous studies and confirmed here to increase LRRK2 activity (Liu et al., 2018; Mir et al., 2018; Purlyte et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and data in the current manuscript.

claim: LRRK2 R1441G and VPS35 D620N variants may promote LRRK2 activation by increasing Rab12-mediated LRRK2 localization to lysosomes.
source: Our results suggest that these variants may also promote LRRK2 activation by increasing Rab12-mediated LRRK2 localization to lysosomes, implying this may represent a general mechanism by which LRRK2 activity is increased by various genetic variants and environmental stressors associated with PD.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the data showing increased LRRK2 on lysosomes in cells expressing these variants.

claim: Increased Rab12-mediated LRRK2 localization to lysosomes may represent a general mechanism by which LRRK2 activity is increased by various genetic variants and environmental stressors associated with PD.
source: Our results suggest that these variants may also promote LRRK2 activation by increasing Rab12-mediated LRRK2 localization to lysosomes, implying this may represent a general mechanism by which LRRK2 activity is increased by various genetic variants and environmental stressors associated with PD.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the data presented.

claim: LRRK2 activity may be upregulated as a compensatory response to restore lysosomal homeostasis following damage.
source: While the purpose of LRRK2 recruitment and activation on lysosomes is poorly defined, several hypotheses have been proposed suggesting that LRRK2 activity may be upregulated as a compensatory response to restore lysosomal homeostasis following damage.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on previous literature.

claim: LRRK2 activity controls the decision to repair minor damage to lysosomal membranes through an ESCRT-mediated process or to target damaged lysosomes for degradation via lysophagy.
source: Previous work supports a model in which LRRK2 activity controls the decision to repair minor damage to lysosomal membranes through an ESCRT-mediated process or to target damaged lysosomes for degradation via lysophagy (Herbst et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: LRRK2 hyperactivation triggers mechanisms aimed at clearing cargo from damaged lysosomes through direct exocytosis of lysosomes or through LYTL.
source: Additional studies suggested that LRRK2 hyperactivation triggers mechanisms aimed at clearing cargo from damaged lysosomes that have lost their proteolytic capacity, either through direct exocytosis of lysosomes or through a novel sorting process termed LYTL (lysosomal tubulation/sorting driven by LRRK2) in which tubules bud off from lysosomes following membrane rupture (Bonet-Ponce et al., 2020; Eguchi et al., 2018; Kluss et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: LRRK2 activation in the face of minor or acute lysosomal insults likely plays a beneficial role in maintaining lysosomal function.
source: LRRK2 activation in the face of minor or acute lysosomal insults likely plays a beneficial role in maintaining lysosomal function, while chronic LRRK2 activation triggered by genetic variants with increased kinase activity or low-level lysosomal damage over time may ultimately impair the ability to effectively respond to membrane stress and maintain the balance between lysosomal repair and destruction.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the authors' interpretation of the data.

claim: Chronic LRRK2 activation triggered by genetic variants with increased kinase activity or low-level lysosomal damage over time may ultimately impair the ability to effectively respond to membrane stress and maintain the balance between lysosomal repair and destruction.
source: LRRK2 activation in the face of minor or acute lysosomal insults likely plays a beneficial role in maintaining lysosomal function, while chronic LRRK2 activation triggered by genetic variants with increased kinase activity or low-level lysosomal damage over time may ultimately impair the ability to effectively respond to membrane stress and maintain the balance between lysosomal repair and destruction.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the authors' interpretation of the data.

claim: Macrophages from PD patients carrying pathogenic LRRK2 variants accumulate more damaged lysosomes compared to samples from healthy controls.
source: Macrophages from PD patients carrying pathogenic LRRK2 variants were shown to accumulate more damaged lysosomes compared to samples from healthy controls, suggesting that mechanisms that respond to and repair lysosomal membrane rupture may be perturbed in PD (Herbst et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Mechanisms that respond to and repair lysosomal membrane rupture may be perturbed in PD.
source: Macrophages from PD patients carrying pathogenic LRRK2 variants were shown to accumulate more damaged lysosomes compared to samples from healthy controls, suggesting that mechanisms that respond to and repair lysosomal membrane rupture may be perturbed in PD (Herbst et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that PD patient macrophages accumulate damaged lysosomes.
